title: Routers for registering
idea: A router maps a method and path to a controller. `auth.routes.js` maps `POST /register` to `registerUser`; `app.js` mounts the router under `/api/v1/auth`.
points: A `Router` groups related routes; the healthcheck route already used one.
`router.route('/register').post(registerUser)` maps one method and path to the controller.
`app.use('/api/v1/auth', authRouter)` mounts it; the router sees only `/register`.
Mount routers below `express.json()`, or the controller finds `req.body` undefined.

parts.label: Method
parts.note: `.post(...)` in the router matches this method only. The same path with `GET` gets `404`.

parts.label: Version prefix
parts.note: Part of the mount path in `app.js`, shared by every route of this API version.

parts.label: Router mount
parts.note: The rest of the mount path in `app.js`. Every route in the auth router starts here.

parts.label: Route
parts.note: Declared in `auth.routes.js`. The router sees only this part of the path.

code.title: src/routes/auth.routes.js
code.caption: The router file. Later lessons put validators and the auth middleware before the controller in this same chain.

code.title: Mount and call
code.caption: Router, mount and three calls in one file. A stand-in controller replies, so the focus stays on the paths.

walk.text: A stand-in for the controller from the last lesson.
`Router()` makes a group of routes. `route('/register').post(...)` maps one method and path.
Mount below the body parser. Every route in the router now starts with `/api/v1/auth`.
Full path and right method: the controller runs.
Same path, other method: no route matches, so Express answers `404`.
Without the `/auth` mount segment nothing matches either.

pitfalls: Write `/register` in the router, not `/auth/register`: the mount adds the prefix.
Pass `registerUser`, not `registerUser()`: calling it runs the controller at startup, not per request.
A router mounted before `express.json()` sees `req.body` as `undefined`.

quiz.why: The first URL has the mount prefix and matches. The second lacks it, so no route matches and Express sends `404`.

takeaway: The router names the route; `app.use` supplies the prefix.

starters: What does `router.route('/register')` do that `router.post('/register')` does not?
Where do validators and middleware go in a route?
